These examples all come down to 2 real affects imo. One is that a more productive economy has more room for workers. Two is that humans' ultimate tool is genralized cognitive flexibility, so we can keep pivoting towards demand. Where this gets sketchy isn't if AI supplants a limited subset of cognitive skills, but if it is superhuman across the board or close to it. What value does your cognitive flexibility provide if a algorithm is better at it and runs for pennies, and it will always arbitrage your labor? What can you offer past that, finger dexterity for a while maybe? Even if creativity is the last domain where humans exceed AI, that is a wildly unequal economy because suddenly the productivity/pay distribution looks like musicians rather than factory workers. But i am pretty optimistic if at the end of it all we still find a pretty wide area where humans excel compared to AI

I think your timeframe is off by about 1000 years. Technology is changing at all exponential rate. We're already seeing AI with human-like capabilities in the creative and social fields. It's easy to say that AI will only shift the job market but AI is not the same as previous breakthroughs. Every breakthrough in the past has still required some human interaction. AI not only does the job in question, but can also do any resulting jobs. The last bastion of human work would be entertainment, but even then, what if an AI is developed that is funnier than any human, or better at telling stories? We need to prepare for a future where humans have no purpose. Maybe AI will assist us with bringing about our wildest dreams, or maybe we will be their neanderthal.

If you are a fresh graduate, you are screwed. If you don't have C1 German, you are screwed. C1 German language here is literally more important than your master's degree in 90% of the situations.
